title: Rama
tomorrow: why would a mother ask God to look less like God?

segments.voice: Yesterday, two wooden sandals on an empty throne: Bharata ruled in his brother's name and waited for him. Rama stays with us one more day, on a beach, at night.

The knock always comes at the worst hour: a text near midnight, a friend on the step with a bag. Rama's comes on a beach. His army is camped on the shore, facing Lanka, and a figure crosses the water through the air with a few companions and calls down. I'm Vibhishana, Ravana's brother. I told him to give Sita back, and he threw me out. I've come to Rama for refuge. The whole camp goes quiet. The enemy's own brother is asking to come in.
screen: `A KNOCK AT THE WORST HOUR.` → `RAVANA'S BROTHER, IN THE SKY.` → `I'VE COME FOR REFUGE.`

segments.voice: In Valmiki's Ramayana, Rama doesn't answer right away. He asks his allies. Sugriva, the monkey king, is wary: this could be a spy, here to learn the plans or strike while they sleep. Others want to test him first, or keep him under guard until the war is won. Every one of those fears is reasonable; it is wartime, and he is Ravana's brother. Hanuman speaks up for him: he chose his moment with care, and he talks like someone who means it. Then Rama answers, and the answer goes past the question. Whoever comes to me even once, he says, and tells me they're mine, I protect from every being. That's my vow. Then he goes further: even if Ravana himself came this way asking, I'd take him in. So Vibhishana is welcomed, and Rama has him anointed, right there, as the future king of Lanka. Here's the part worth telling someone tonight. The camp was asking: is he safe for us? Rama answered a different question: who am I? A refuge that only opens for the safe guest isn't much of a refuge. And a vow that has to be re-voted every night isn't much of a vow. The Bhagavata Purana retells this war too, and the Rama these weeks have followed is this one, whose door stays open even to the enemy's brother.
screen: `RAMA ASKS HIS ALLIES FIRST.` · `A SPY? OR SOMEONE WHO MEANS IT?` · `ANYONE WHO COMES ONCE, I PROTECT.` · `EVEN RAVANA, IF HE CAME.` · then, large: `THE DOOR STAYS OPEN.`

segments.voice: Sit up, and rest your hands open on your knees, palms up, like a door already unlocked. Each time you breathe out, let your shoulders drop and keep the hands open. Nothing to check and nothing to guard, for the whole sit.
Rama: the prince of Ayodhya, in the Puranas Vishnu come as a man, whose vow was to shelter anyone who comes asking.
Your line: Rama. Even Ravana, he said, would be taken in if he came asking. Back tomorrow.
